message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.16","text":"Nevertheless, there are many heralds of error, all having one leader of wickedness. For that reason there is one herald of the truth, himself also the leader of piety, who in their proper times will have as prophets all who are found pure. The chief reason people have gone astray has been this: they did not first understand the principle of pairing, which I will not cease setting out for you separately, on each occasion, in outline; for speaking point by point is a lengthy task. Therefore, be truth-loving judges for me of what is said.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ᾧ λόγῳ τῆς ἀληθείας εἷς","chosen":"For that reason there is one herald of the truth","rationale":"The singular noun is implicit from the preceding κήρυκες; “for that reason” renders the causal ᾧ λόγῳ."},{"source_quote":"ἐν ἰδίοις καιροῖς","chosen":"in their proper times","rationale":"The phrase is taken with the prophets as referring to their respective times; attachment to the singular herald remains possible."},{"source_quote":"τὸν τῆς συζυγίας λόγον","chosen":"the principle of pairing","rationale":"λόγος denotes an account or principle, while συζυγία is the work’s technical language for a paired relation; “doctrine of the pairs” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ἑκάστοτε","chosen":"on each occasion","rationale":"The adverb indicates recurrence on every relevant occasion, rather than merely occurring from time to time."},{"source_quote":"κεφαλαιωδῶς","chosen":"in outline","rationale":"The adverb indicates a summary treatment by principal points rather than a full exposition."},{"source_quote":"πολὺ γὰρ τὸ κατ᾽ εἶδος λέγειν","chosen":"for speaking point by point is a lengthy task","rationale":"κατ᾽ εἶδος means treating the matter specifically or item by item, while πολύ indicates its considerable extent."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἰδία","issue":"The image-checked edition prints ἰδία, a morphologically unexpected form in this adverbial position. The translation provisionally understands it as “separately” or “privately”; the printed form is preserved and is not treated as an OCR error.","proposed_reading":"ἰδίᾳ","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.17","text":"I will now begin speaking. If someone refuses to grant that the great and holy spirit of the foreknowledge of God, who made all things, was infused into the man brought to term by his hands, how does the person who assigns it to another—one born from a foul drop—not sin most gravely? I do not think that person obtains forgiveness, even if he is deceived by spurious scripture into thinking dreadful things against the father of all. For anyone who insults an image—and an eternal king’s image at that—commits that sin against the one in whose likeness the image happened to be. “But,” he says, “the divine spirit left him after he sinned.” Then it sinned along with him. And how is the one who says this not in danger? “No, he had received the spirit after he sinned.” Then it has been given to unrighteous people. And where is justice? “But it is supplied to righteous and unrighteous alike.” This is the most unjust thing of all. Thus every falsehood, even if supported by ten thousand contrivances, is bound to meet its refutation even within a short time.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῷ ὑπὸ χειρῶν αὐτοῦ κυοφορηθέντι ἀνθρώπῳ","chosen":"into the man brought to term by his hands","rationale":"κυοφορέω carries a gestational image, here paradoxically associated with God’s hands; “formed by his hands” would suppress that image."},{"source_quote":"δῴη τις ἐγχέναι","chosen":"refuses to grant that ... was infused","rationale":"The construction leaves the agency of the active infinitive ἐγχέναι implicit. The passive English keeps the spirit as what is infused without supplying an explicit agent; “grant that God infused” is a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ νόθου γραφῆς","chosen":"by spurious scripture","rationale":"νόθος marks the writing as illegitimate or inauthentic, and γραφή in this context can denote a purported scriptural writing; “spurious writing” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ταῦτα αἰωνίου βασιλέως","chosen":"and an eternal king’s image at that","rationale":"καὶ ταῦτα is an emphatic idiom highlighting the especially serious identity of the person represented by the image."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ἁμαρτίαν εἰς ἐκεῖνον ἀναφερομένην ἔχει, οὗπερ καθ᾽ ὁμοίωσιν ἡ εἰκὼν ἐτύγχανεν οὖσα","chosen":"commits that sin against the one in whose likeness the image happened to be","rationale":"The sin is directed against the person represented by the insulted image; the wording does not transfer the offender’s culpability to that person. More literally, one “has the sin referred against that one.”"},{"source_quote":"οὐκοῦν συνήμαρτεν","chosen":"Then it sinned along with him","rationale":"The compound verb presents the spirit as sharing in the man’s sin, which is the reductio advanced by the author."},{"source_quote":"κἂν μυρίαις ἐπινοίαις βοηθῆται","chosen":"even if supported by ten thousand contrivances","rationale":"The rendering preserves μυρίαις as “ten thousand,” though it can idiomatically mean “countless,” and takes ἐπίνοιαι as devised arguments or contrivances."},{"source_quote":"τὸν ἔλεγχον κἂν ἐν μικρῷ χρόνῳ λαβεῖν ἔχει","chosen":"is bound to meet its refutation even within a short time","rationale":"ἔχει with the infinitive expresses an assured outcome, and ἔλεγχος here is exposure or refutation."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.18","text":"Do not be deceived. Our father was ignorant of nothing, since even the law laid down publicly, while concealing him beneath a veil of allegory because of the unworthy, refers those who yearn for truth back to him, saying, “Examine your father, and he will tell you; your elders, and they will report to you.” It was this father one had to seek, these elders one had to seek out. But you did not seek to learn to whom the time of the kingdom belongs, or to whom the chair of prophecy belongs, even though he disclosed himself by saying, “The scribes and the Pharisees sat on Moses’ chair. Everything they tell you, listen to them.” He said “them” because they had been entrusted with the key of the kingdom, which is knowledge. It alone can open the gate of life, and through it alone it is possible to enter eternal life. “But yes,” he says, “they possess the key, yet they do not provide it to those who wish to enter.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν","chosen":"our father","rationale":"The designation is retained without inserting a name or capitalizing it, since the immediate wording does not make the referent explicit."},{"source_quote":"ἀλληγορίας ἐγκαλύμματι","chosen":"beneath a veil of allegory","rationale":"ἐγκάλυμμα is a covering or veil, and the law is depicted as concealing the father through allegorical presentation."},{"source_quote":"ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἀναπέμπει","chosen":"refers ... back to him","rationale":"ἀναπέμπω can mean sending or referring someone back to another person or authority."},{"source_quote":"τίνος ἐστὶν ὁ τῆς βασιλείας χρόνος, τίνος ἡ τῆς προφητείας καθέδρα","chosen":"to whom the time of the kingdom belongs, or to whom the chair of prophecy belongs","rationale":"The repeated genitive τίνος asks whose these prerogatives are; the English supplies “belongs” without identifying the person."},{"source_quote":"τὴν κλεῖδα τῆς βασιλείας πεπιστευμένων","chosen":"they had been entrusted with the key of the kingdom","rationale":"The passive perfect of πιστεύω here means being entrusted with something, not merely believing it."},{"source_quote":"ἥτις ἐστὶν γνῶσις, ἡ μόνη τὴν πύλην τῆς ζωῆς ἀνοῖξαι δύναται, δι’ ἧς μόνης","chosen":"which is knowledge. It alone can open the gate of life, and through it alone","rationale":"The repeated feminine forms are taken as referring to knowledge. Because πύλη is also feminine and nearer to δι’ ἧς, “through which gate alone” remains grammatically possible."},{"source_quote":"ἀλλὰ ναί","chosen":"But yes","rationale":"The emphatic response concedes possession of the key before contrasting the refusal to provide it."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.19","text":"For this reason, I say, he himself rose from the chair. Like a father acting on behalf of children, he proclaimed what had from eternity been handed down secretly to the worthy; he extended mercy even to the nations and had compassion on the souls of all, while disregarding his own blood. For he, having been deemed worthy to be king of the coming age, against the one who had now received the kingdom under a time-limited law.... And the greatest thing, which distressed him intensely, is this: those on whose behalf he waged the battle as for children were themselves fighting against him because of ignorance. And yet he loved even those who hated him, wept for those who disobeyed, blessed those who reviled him, and prayed for those who treated him as an enemy. He did not do only these things as a father, but also taught his own disciples to do similar things with the attitude they would have toward brothers. This is a father; this is a prophet; this is what is fitting: for him to reign over his own children, so that through the affection that goes from a father to children and the children’s heartfelt honor toward their father, eternal peace might be able to arise. For when the fitting ruler reigns, genuine joy concerning the ruler comes upon those who are ruled.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"αὐτὸς τῆς καθέδρας ἐγερθείς","chosen":"he himself rose from the chair","rationale":"The wording continues the chair imagery of the preceding section; ἐγερθείς is rendered as rising from it rather than merely being raised up."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ἀπὸ αἰῶνος ἐν κρυπτῷ ἀξίοις παραδιδόμενα","chosen":"what had from eternity been handed down secretly to the worthy","rationale":"ἀπὸ αἰῶνος may also mean “from of old” or “from the beginning of the age”; the rendering retains its broad temporal force without supplying a starting event."},{"source_quote":"ἰδίου αἵματος ἠμέλει","chosen":"disregarding his own blood","rationale":"The literal image is retained. It may refer to accepting the shedding of his blood or, more generally, neglecting his own life and safety."},{"source_quote":"ἐνπροθέσμῳ ... νόμῳ","chosen":"under a time-limited law","rationale":"The compound denotes something governed by a fixed term or deadline; “under a law with a fixed term” is a more literal alternative."},{"source_quote":"ὑπ’ αὐτῶν ἀγνοίας αἰτίᾳ ἐπολεμεῖτο","chosen":"were themselves fighting against him because of ignorance","rationale":"The passive verb depicts him as the object of their hostility, while ἀγνοίας αἰτίᾳ gives ignorance as its cause."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς αὐτοῦ μαθηταῖς ὡς πρὸς ἀδελφοὺς ἔχοντας τὰ ὅμοια ποιεῖν ἐδίδασκεν","chosen":"taught his own disciples to do similar things with the attitude they would have toward brothers","rationale":"The main rendering understands ἔχειν πρός relationally, with ὡς preserving the comparison to conduct toward brothers. Alternatively, ἔχοντας with the infinitive may express obligation: “taught his disciples that they had to do similar things as toward brothers.”"},{"source_quote":"τοῦτο εὔλογον ... τοῦ γὰρ εὐλόγου βασιλεύοντος","chosen":"this is what is fitting ... when the fitting ruler reigns","rationale":"The repeated εὔλογος language can mean reasonable, fitting, or rightful. “Fitting” connects the claim that he should reign with the character of his rule; “when a reasonable ruler reigns” is also possible."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὴν βασιλείαν.... καὶ","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly four dots after βασιλείαν, leaving the preceding construction without its unavailable continuation. The English retains all four dots, and no restoration has been supplied.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐνπροθέσμῳ","issue":"The image-checked edition prints ἐνπροθέσμῳ, apparently an unassimilated or irregular spelling of the compound ordinarily written with μ before π. Its meaning remains recoverable, but this interpretation is provisional and the form is not treated as an OCR error.","proposed_reading":"ἐμπροθέσμῳ","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.20","text":"Nevertheless, I return to the first argument concerning the truth. If someone does not grant that the man brought to term by God’s hands has the Messiah’s holy spirit, how is he not committing the greatest impiety by granting that some other person, born from a foul drop, has it? Rather, he acts with the greatest piety if he does not grant that another has it, but says that that one alone has it—the one who, from the beginning of the age, changing forms together with names, courses through the age until, having reached his own times and having been anointed by God’s mercy because of his labors, he will have rest forever. That one has been honored with ruling and exercising dominion over everything in air, on earth, and in waters. In addition, he received the breath of the very one who made man—an unbreakable covering for the soul—so that he might be able to be immortal.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸ ἅγιον χριστοῦ ... πνεῦμα","chosen":"the Messiah’s holy spirit","rationale":"χριστός functions independently as a title, so it is rendered “Messiah.” The genitive relates the spirit to the Messiah without deciding whether possession, identity, or source is foremost; “the holy spirit of Christ” is an alternative form."},{"source_quote":"τῷ ὑπὸ χειρῶν θεοῦ κυοφορηθέντι ἀνθρώπῳ","chosen":"the man brought to term by God’s hands","rationale":"The rendering retains the unusual gestational force of κυοφορηθέντι together with the explicit image of God’s hands."},{"source_quote":"ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς αἰῶνος ... τὸν αἰῶνα τρέχει","chosen":"from the beginning of the age ... courses through the age","rationale":"The repeated rendering preserves the source’s repetition of αἰών and its portrayal of movement throughout the age."},{"source_quote":"ἅμα τοῖς ὀνόμασιν μορφὰς ἀλλάσσων","chosen":"changing forms together with names","rationale":"Both changing forms and corresponding names are retained without identifying particular manifestations not named here."},{"source_quote":"διὰ τοὺς καμάτους θεοῦ ἐλέει χρισθείς","chosen":"having been anointed by God’s mercy because of his labors","rationale":"χρισθείς is rendered “anointed” to preserve its relation to the title Messiah, while διά with the accusative gives the labors as the reason; “on account of his toils” is an alternative."},{"source_quote":"ἄρχειν τε καὶ κυριεύειν ... τετίμηται","chosen":"has been honored with ruling and exercising dominion","rationale":"The two infinitives preserve the distinction between governing and holding dominion as the honor granted to him."},{"source_quote":"τὴν πνοὴν ἔσχεν, ψυχῆς ἄρρηκτον περιβολήν","chosen":"he received the breath ... an unbreakable covering for the soul","rationale":"The second phrase is taken in apposition to the breath. The genitive ψυχῆς may alternatively be rendered “an unbreakable covering of the soul,” but the context supports a covering bestowed upon and protecting the soul."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
